questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses $\mathrm{m}_1$ and $\mathrm{m}_2$ (where $m_2 > m_1$). If the acceleration of the system is $\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\sqrt{2}}$, then the ratio of the masses $\frac{m_1}{m_2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration is given as:
a= $\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right)$g\Rightarrow $\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\sqrt{2}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{m}_2-\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right) \mathrm{g}\Rightarrow \sqrt{2}\left($m_2-m_1\right)=m_1+m_2\Rightarrow $\frac{\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_2}=$$\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass 1 kg is pushed up a surface inclined to horizontal at an angle of $60^{{}^{\circ}}$ by a force of 10 N parallel to the inclined surface as shown in figure. When the block is pushed up by 10 m along inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is : $\left[g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right]$
questions.solution:
Mass of block, $m=1 \mathrm{ kg}$
Force of parallel inclined surface, $\mathrm{F}=10 \mathrm{ N}$
Work done against frictional force
$=\mu_2 \mathrm{ N} \times 10=\mu \mathrm{Mg} \cos 60 \times 10=0.1 \times 5 \times 10=5 \mathrm{ J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person of mass 60 kg is inside a lift of mass 940 kg and presses the button on control panel. The lift starts moving upwards with an acceleration $1.0 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. If $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$, the tension in the supporting cable is
questions.solution: Total mass $=(60+940) \mathrm{kg}=1000 \mathrm{ kg}$ Let T be the tension in the supporting cable, then $T-1000 g=1000 \times 1\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}=1000 \times 11=11000 \mathrm{ N}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At any instant the velocity of a particle of mass $500 \mathrm{~g}$ is $\left(2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}\right) \mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$. If the force acting on the particle at $t=1 s$ is $(\hat{i}+x \hat{j}) N$. Then the value of $\mathrm{x}$ will be:
questions.solution:
Mass of particle, $\mathrm{m}=500 \mathrm{ g}=0.5 \mathrm{ kg}$
velocity of a particle, $\vec{v}=2 t \hat{i}+3 t^2 \hat{j}$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\mathrm{d} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \mathrm{t} \hat{\mathrm{j}}$
at $\mathrm{t}=1, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}}$
Force acting on the particle,
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=\mathrm{ma}=0.5(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+6 \hat{\mathrm{j}})=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}$
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+x \hat{\mathrm{j}} \quad$ Hence $x=3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the diagram shown below, both the strings $A B$ and $C D$ are made of same material and have same cross-section. The pulleys are light and fictionless. If the speed of wave in string $A B$ is $v_1$ and in $C D$ is $v_2$, then $\frac{v_1}{v_2}$ is
questions.solution: Let the speed of wave in string be $v$ and tension in string be $T$. $\begin{gathered}$ v \propto $\sqrt{T}\\ \frac{v_{A B}}{v_{C D}}=\sqrt{\frac{T}{2 T}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: What will be the acceleration due to gravity at a depth $d$, where $g$ is acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth?
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity at the surface of earth,

g=$\frac{G M}{R^2}=\frac{4}{3} \pi \rho$G R

$\left[\because$M=$\frac{4}{3} \pi$R^3 $\cdot \rho\right]$Where, $\rho=$ density of earth.
Acceleration due to gravity at depth $d from the surface of $earth,

g^{\prime}=$\frac{4}{3} \pi \rhoG(R-d)$ From Eqs. (i) and(ii), we get

g^{\prime}=g$\left[$1-$\frac{d}{R}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with velocity $v$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. At its highest point, it explodes into two pieces of equal mass, one of the piece continue to move on the original trajectory, then the velocity of second piece is
questions.solution: According to the law of conservation of linear momentum at the highest point, m v \cos $\theta=\frac{m}{2}(v \cos \theta)+\frac{m}{2}$ v^{\prime} $\Rightarrow \quad m v \cos \theta-\frac{m}{2} v \cos \theta=\frac{m}{2} v^{\prime}\Rightarrow \quad v^{\prime}=2\left(v \cos \theta-\frac{v \cos \theta}{2}\right)=v \cos \theta$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of weight $2 \mathrm{ kg}$ is suspended as shown in the figure. The tension $\mathrm{T}_{1}$ in the horizontal string (in $\mathrm{kg}$ wt ) is
questions.solution:
The tension in the above string can be divided into two components where the component opposite to weight will balance the weight while the component of this tension opposite to \($\mathrm{T}_{1}$\) will be equal to \($\mathrm{T}_{1}$\).

\($\mathrm{T} \sin \theta=$2 $\mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{wt}$\)

\($\mathrm{T} \cos \theta=\mathrm{T}_{1}$\)

The first equation gives

\($\mathrm{T}=$4 $\mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{wt}$\)

So \($\mathrm{T}_{1}$\) will be,

\($\mathrm{T}_{1}=$2 $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{wt}$\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball of mass $0.2 \mathrm{~kg}$ is thrown vertically upwards by applying a force by hand. If the hand moves $0.2 \mathrm{~m}$ while applying the force and the ball goes upto $2 \mathrm{~m}$ height further, find the magnitude of the force. (Consider $\left.g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrms^{2}\right)$.
questions.solution: Let the velocity of the ball just when it leaves the hand is $u$ then applying, $$\begin{array}{l} v^{2}-u^{2}=2 a $\text{$ for upward journey } \\ \Rightarrow-u^{2}=2(-10) \times 2 \\ \Rightarrow u^{2}=40 \end{array}$ Again applying $v^{2}-u^{2}=2 a s$ for the upward journey of the ball, when the ball is in the hands of the thrower, $\begin{array}{l}v^{2}-u^{2}=2 a s \\ \Rightarrow 40-0=2(a) 0.2 \\ \Rightarrow a=100 $\mathrm{~m}$/ \mathrms^{2} \\ \therefore $\mathrm{F}=$m a=0.2 \times100=20 $\mathrm{~N}$\\ \Rightarrow $\mathrm{N}-$m g=20 \\ \Rightarrow $\mathrm{N}=$20+2=22 $\mathrm{~N}$ \end{array}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The upper half of an inclined plane with inclination $\phi$ is perfectlysmooth while the lower halfis rough. A body starting from rest at the top will again come to rest at the bottom if the coefficient of friction for the lower half is given by
questions.solution: Acceleration of block while sliding down upper half $=\mathrm{g} \sin \phi$ retardation of block while sliding down lower half $=-(\mathrm{g} \sin \phi-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \phi)$ For the block to come to rest at the bottom, acceleration in I half = retardation in II half. $\mathrm{g} \sin \phi=-(\mathrm{g} \sin \phi-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \phi)\Rightarrow \mu=2 \tan \phi$ Alternative method: According to work-energy theorem, $\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{K}=0$ (Since initial and final speeds are zero) $\therefore$ Work done by friction $+$ Work done by gravity $=0$ i.e., $-(\mu \mathrm{mg} \cos \phi) \frac{\ell}{2}+\mathrm{mg} \ell \sin \phi=0$ or $\frac{\mu}{2} \cos \phi=\sin \phi$ or $\mu=2 \tan \phi$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The coefficient of friction between the rubber tyres and the road wayis $0.25 .$ The maximum speed with which a car can be driven round a curve of radius $20 \mathrm{~m}$ without skidding is $\left(\mathrm{g}=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrms^{2}\right)$
questions.solution: $\mu \mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{mv}^{2} / \mathrm{r}$ or $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\mu \mathrm{g} \mathrm{r}}$ or $v=\sqrt{(0.25 \times 9.8 \times 20)}=7 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $2 \mathrm{~kg}$ is placed on a horizontal surface having kinetic friction 0.4 and static friction $0.5 .$ If the force applied on the body is $2.5 \mathrm{~N},$ then the frictional force acting on the body will be $\left[\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-2}\right]$
questions.solution: Limiting friction $=0.5 \times 2 \times 10=10 \mathrm{ N}$ The applied force is less than force of friction, therefore the force of friction is equal to the applied force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass $m$ is moving in a straight line with momentum $p$. Starting at time $t = 0$, a force $F = at$ acts in the same direction on the moving particle during time interval of $T$. So that its momentum changes from $p$ to $2p$. The value of $T$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $F = at$

when, $t = 0$, then linear momentum $= p$

when, $t = T$,~then linear momentum $= 2p$

According to Newton's law of motion, applied force, $F = \dfrac{dp}{dt}$

or~$dp = Fdt$

$dp = atdt$

or~${∫}_p^{2p}dp = a{∫}_{0}^{T}tdt$

$\left(2p - p\right) = a \cdot \dfrac{T2}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2p}{a} = T^{2} ⇒ T = \sqrt{\dfrac{2p}{a}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A maximum of $3N$~force can be applied on& a& block, down the incline, that& would still& not& move the block which is& placed on a rough inclined plane as shown in the figure. The maximum external force up the inclined plane that does not move the block is $12N$. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the plane is $\left[Takeg = 10ms^{- 2}\right]$
questions.solution:
Block does not move upto a maximum applied force of $3N$down the inclined plane.

Equation of motion is $3 + mgsin30 ° = F$

$3 + mgsin30 ° = \mumgcos30 °$ & & & & &....(i)

Similarly, block also does not move upto a maximum applied force of $12N$ up the plane.

Now, equation of motion is

$mgsin30 ° + F = 12$

or, $mgsin30 ° + \mumgcos30 ° = 12$ & & & & &...(ii)

Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii), we have

$mgsin30 ° = \dfrac{9}{2}$ and $\mumgcos30 ° = \dfrac{15}{2}$

Hence, dividing

$∴ \dfrac{1}{μ}tan30 ° = \dfrac{9 / 2}{15 / 2} = \dfrac{3}{5}$

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{5}{3\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The force on a body of mass $1$ kg is~$\left(20\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j}\right)N$. If it starts from rest, then the position of the body at time $t = 2s,$& is
questions.solution:
$F = 20\overset{^}{i} + 10\overset{^}{j}$

$∴ {F}_{x} = 20N$ and ${F}_{y} = 10N$

$∴$ Acceleration,

${a}_{x} = \dfrac{Fx}{m} = \dfrac{20}{1}$
${a}_{x} = 20ms^{- 2}$

and ${a}_{y} = \dfrac{Fy}{m} = \dfrac{10}{1} = 10ms^{- 2}$

$∴$ Displacement of body in $x$ -direction in $2s$.

$x = {u}_{x}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{x}t^{2}$

$= 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times {2}^{2}$
$= 40m$

Displacement of body in $y$-direction in $2s$.

$y = {u}_{y}t + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{y}t^{2}$

$= 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {2}^{2}$

$= 20m$

$∴$ Position of the body at $t = 2s$

$r = x\overset{^}{i} + y\overset{^}{j}$
$r = 40\overset{^}{i} + 20\overset{^}{j}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An automobile moving with a speed of $36kmh^{- 1}$ reaches an upward inclined road of angle $30 ° ,$ its engine becomes switch off. If the coefficient of friction is $0. 1$, then how much distance will automobile move before coming to rest?
questions.solution:
Given, initial speed, $u = 36kmh^{- 1}$

$= \dfrac{36 \times 1000}{60 \times 60} = 10ms^{- 1}$

$\theta = 30 ° , \mu = 0 . 1, s = ?$

Here, work done in moving up the inclined road$= KE$ of the vehicle

$\left(mgsin\theta + F\right)s = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

$\left(mgsin\theta + \muR\right) \times s = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

$\left(mgsin\theta + \mumgcos\theta\right) \times s = \dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}$

$s = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}mu^{2}}{mg\left(sin\theta + \mucos\theta\right)} = \dfrac{u2}{2g\left(sin\theta + \mucos\theta\right)}$

$= \dfrac{10 \times 10}{2 \times 10 \times \left(sin30 ° + 0 . 1cos30 °\right)} = 8 . 53m$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object takes $n$ times as much time to slide down a $45 °$ rough inclined plane as it takes to slide down a perfectly smooth $45 °$ inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rough plane and the object is
questions.solution:
$s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}, a = gsin\theta, u = 0$

Then, $s = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$

or $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{gsin\theta}}$ [for smooth plane]

For the rough plane. the effective value of acceleration along the incline is
$a^{'} = gsin\theta - {μ}_{k}gcos\theta$

and $t^{'} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{gsin\theta - {μ}_{k}gcos\theta}}$

Now, $\dfrac{t '}{t} = n = \sqrt{\dfrac{gsin\theta}{gsin\theta - {μ}_{k}gcos\theta}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{sin45 °}{sin45 ° - {μ}_{k}cos45 °}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{1 - {μ}_{k}}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{n2} = 1 - {μ}_{k} ⇒ {μ}_{k} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two blocks $A$ and $B$ are placed one over the other on a smooth horizontal surface. The maximum horizontal force that can be applied on lower block $A$, so that $A$ and $B$ move without separation is $49N$. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
Equation of motion of lower block is

$F = \mu\left({M}_{A} + {M}_{B}\right) \cdot g$

$\mu = \dfrac{F}{\left({M}_{A} + {M}_{B}\right)g}$

$= \dfrac{49}{10 \times 9. 8} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0. 5$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block $A$ of mass $100$ kg rests on another block $B$ of mass $200$ kg and is tied to a wall as shown in the figure. The coefficient of friction between $A and B$ is $0 . 2$ and that between $B$ and ground is $0 . 3$. The minimum force required to move the block $B$ is $\left(g = 10ms^{- 2}\right)$
questions.solution:
Friction force between $A$ and $B$ and between block $B$ and surface $S$ will oppose $F$

$∴ F = {F}_{AB} + {F}_{BS} = {μ}_{AB}{M}_{A}g + {μ}_{BS}\left({m}_{A} + {m}_{B}\right)g$

$= 0. 2 \times 100 \times 10 + 0. 3\left(100 + 200\right) \times 10$

$= 200 + 900 = 1100N$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Block A of mass $\mathrm{m}$ and block $\mathrm{B}$ of mass $2 \mathrm{ m}$ are placed on a fixed triangular wedge by means of a massless, inextensible string and a frictionless pulley as shown in figure.
The wedge is inclined at $45^{{}^{\circ}}$ to the horizontal on both the sides. If the coefficient of friction between the block $\mathrm{A}$ and the wedge is $2 / 3$ and that between the block $\mathrm{B}$ and the wedge is $1 / 3$ and both the blocks $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are released from rest, the acceleration of A will be
questions.solution:
Total maximum friction force,\(f_{t}=f_{A}+f_{B}\)

\(\mu_{\mathrm{A}}\mathrm{mg} \cos$45^{{}^{\circ}}+\mu_{\mathrm{B}}$ 2 $\mathrm{mg} \cos$45^{{}^{\circ}}\)

or, \(f_{t}=m g$\left(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{3} \times$2 $\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$

\(=$\frac{4}{3 \sqrt{2}} \mathrm{mg} The $net pulling force, \(F=2 m g \sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}-m g \sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}\) \(=$\mathrm{mg} \sin$45^{{}^{\circ}}\)

\(=$\frac{m g}{\sqrt{2}}$

\(\because $\mathrm{F}\lt \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{t}}$

\(\therefore\) The blocks will not move.

So, acceleration of block A is Zero.

\(\therefore\) option (D) is correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A frictionless wire $\mathrm{AB}$ is fixed on a sphere of radius $\mathrm{R}$. A very small spherical ball slips on this wire. The time taken by this ball to slip from A to $\mathrm{B}$ is
questions.solution: Acceleration of body along $\mathrm{AB}$ is g $\cos \theta$ Distance travelled in time $\mathrm{t}$ sec $=A B=\frac{1}{2}(g \cos \theta) t^{2}$ From $\Delta \mathrm{ABC}, \mathrm{AB}=2 \mathrm{R} \cos \theta$ Thus, $2 \mathrm{R} \cos \theta=\frac{1}{2} g \cos \theta t^{2}\Rightarrow t^{2}=\frac{4 R}{g} \Rightarrow t=2 \sqrt{\frac{R}{g}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In figure, two blocks are separated by a uniform strut attached to each block with frictionless pins. Block $A$ weighs $400 \mathrm{ N}$, block $B$ weighs $300 \mathrm{ N}$, and the strut $A B$ weigh $200 \mathrm{ N}$. If $\mu=0.25$ under $B,$ determine the minimum coefficient of friction under $A$ to prevent motion.
questions.solution:
Consider FBD of structure.
Applying equilibrium equations, $A v+B v=200 \mathrm{ N}A_{H}=B_{H} \ldots$ (ii) From FBD of block $B$,
$B_{H}+F_{B} \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}-N_{B} \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}=0N_{B} \cos 60^{{}^{\circ}}-B_{V}-300+F_{B} \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}=0F_{B}=0.25 N_{B}B_{H}-0.74 N_{B}=0$ (iii) $-B_{V}+0.71 N_{B}=300$ FBD of block $A$
$F_{A}-A_{H}=0N_{A}-A_{V}=400 \quad \ldotsF_{A}=\mu_{A} N_{A}\therefore \mu_{A} N_{A}-A_{H}=0 \quad \ldots$ on solving the above equation $N_{A}=650 \mathrm{ N}, F_{A}=260 \mathrm{ N}, F_{A}=\mu_{A} N_{A}\therefore \mu_{A}=\frac{260}{250}=0.4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The masses of blocks $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are $\mathrm{m}$ and $\mathrm{M}$ respectively. Between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$, there is a constant frictional force $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ can slide on a smooth horizontal surface. A is set in motion with velocity while $\mathrm{B}$ is at rest. What is the distance moved by A relative to B before they move with the same velocity?
questions.solution:
For the blocks A and B FBD as shown below
Equations of motion $\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}(\text{ in }-\mathrm{x} \text{ direction })$\\ $\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}(\text{ in }+\mathrm{x} \text{ direction) } \end{array}$ Relative acceleration, of A w.r.t. B, $\begin{aligned}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}}$&=$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{B}}=-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}-\frac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{M}}$\\ &=-$\mathrm{F}\left(\frac{\mathrm{M}+\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{Mm}}\right)(\text{ along }-\mathrm{x} \text{ direction }) \end{aligned}$ Initial relative velocity of A w.r.t. B, $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\mathrm{v}_{0}$ using equation $v^{2}=u^{2}+2$ as 0=v_{0}^{2}-$\frac{2 \mathrm{ F}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{M}) \mathrm{S}}{\mathrm{Mm}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{S}=\frac{\mathrm{Mmv}_{0}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ F}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{M})}$ i.e., Distance moved by A relative to B $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{\mathrm{Mmv}_{0}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{ F}(\mathrm{ m}+\mathrm{M})}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A load of mass m falls from a height h on to the scale pan hung from the spring as shown in the figure. If the spring constant is $\mathrm{k}$ and mass of the scale pan is zero and the mass $\mathrm{m}$ does not bounce relative to the pan, then the amplitude of vibration is
questions.solution: According to energy conservation principle, If, $\mathrm{x}_{1}$ is maximum elongation in the spring when the particle is in its lowest extreme position. Then, $\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{mgh}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{kx}_{1}^{2}-\mathrm{mgx}_{1}$\\ \Rightarrow $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{kx}_{1}^{2}-\mathrm{mgx}_{1}-\mathrm{mgh}=0 \\ \text{ or, } \mathrm{x}_{1}^{2}-\frac{2 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{x}_{1}-\frac{2 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}} \cdot \mathrm{h}=0 \\ \therefore \mathrm{x}_{1}=\frac{\frac{2 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}} \pm \sqrt{\left.\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}}\right)^{2}+4 \times \frac{2 \mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{h}\right]}}{2} \end{array}$ Amplitude $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{X}_{1}-\mathrm{X}_{0}$ (elongation in spring for equilibrium position) $\mathrm{A}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{k}} \sqrt{\left(1+\frac{2 \mathrm{hk}}{\mathrm{mg}}\right)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A person with his hand in his pocket is skating on ice at the rate of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and describes a circle of radius $50 \mathrm{~m}$. What is his inclination to vertical:

$\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec}^{2}\right)$
questions.solution: Since surface (ice) is frictionless, so the centripetal force required for skating will be provided by inclination of boy with the vertical and that angle is given as $\tan \theta=\frac{\mathrmv^{2}}{\mathrm{rg}}$ where $\mathrm{v}$ is speed of skating $\ $ i is radius of circle in which he moves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The minimum velocity (in $\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ ) with which a car driver must traverse a flat curve of radius $150 \mathrm{ m}$ and coefficient of friction 0.6 to avoid skidding is
questions.solution: The condition to avoid skidding, $\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\mu \mathrm{rg}}=\sqrt{0.6 \times 150 \times 10}=30 \mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bob is hanging over a pulley inside a car through, a string. The second end of the string is in the hand of a person standing in the car. The car is moving with constant acceleration 'a' directed horizontallyas shown in figure. Other end of the string is pulled with constant acceleration 'a' vertically. The tension in the string is equal to -
questions.solution: Applying Newton's law along string \Rightarrow $\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{m} \sqrt{\mathrmg^{2}+\mathrma^{2}}=\mathrm{ma}$ or $\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{m} \sqrt{\mathrmg^{2}+\mathrma^{2}}+\mathrm{ma}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass m is placed on a smooth inclined wedge $A B C$ of inclination $\theta$ as shown in the figure. The wedge is given an acceleration 'a' towards the right. The relation between a and $\theta$ for the block to remain stationary on the wedge is
questions.solution:
Let the mass of block is m. It will remains stationary if forces acting on it are in equilibrium. i.e., $m a \cos \theta=m g \sin \theta\Rightarrow a=g \tan \theta$
Here $\mathrm{ma}=$ Pseudo force on block, $\mathrm{mg}=$ weight

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object experiences a net force and accelerates from rest to its final position in $16 \mathrm{ s}$. How long would the object take to reach the same final position from rest if the object's mass was four times larger ?
questions.solution: When the mass increases by a factor of 4 the acceleration must decrease by a factor of four if the same force is applied. The question asks about position so we need to relate acceleration and time to position. We can do this by the equation $: x_{f}-x_{i}=v_{x i} t+1 / 2 a_{x} t^{2}$ We want the change in position to stay the same. The initial velocity is zero so in order for the change in position to remain constant the term $(1 / 2)$ at ^{2}$ must remain the same. If the acceleration is reduced by a factor of 4 you can see that the time must be increased by a factor of 2 in order for the term to remain the same.$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three blocks of masses $\mathrm{m}_{1}, \mathrm{ m}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{3}$ are connected by massless strings, as shown, on a frictionless table. They are pulled with a force $\mathrm{T}_{3}=40 \mathrm{ N}$. If $m_{1}=10 \mathrm{ kg}, \mathrm{ m}_{2}=6 \mathrm{ kg}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{3}=4 \mathrm{ kg},$ the tension $\mathrm{T}_{2}$ will be
questions.solution:
For equilibrium of all 3 masses, a=$\frac{\mathrm{T}_{3}}{\mathrm{ m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}+\mathrm{m}_{3}}$ For equilibrium of $\mathrm{m}_{1} \ \text{ and } \mathrm{ m}_{2}\mathrm{T}_{2}=\left(\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}\right) \cdot \mathrm{a}$ or, $\mathrm{T}_{2}=\frac{\left(\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}\right) \mathrm{T}_{3}}{\mathrm{ m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}+\mathrm{m}_{3}}$
Given $m_{1}=10 \mathrm{ kg}, \mathrm{ m}_{2}=6 \mathrm{ kg}, \mathrm{ m}_{3}=4 \mathrm{ kg}\mathrm{T}_{3}=40 \mathrm{ N}\therefore \mathrm{T}_{2}=\frac{(10+6) \cdot 40}{10+6+4}=32 \mathrm{ N}$

questions.q:
Two blocks are connected over a massless pulley as shown in fig. The mass of block $A$ is $10 \mathrm{ kg}$ and the coefficient of kinetic
friction is 0.2. Block A slides down the incline at constant speed. The mass of block $\mathrm{B}$ in $\mathrm{kg}$ is:

Considering the equilibrium of A, we get $\begin{array}{l}10 \mathrm{a}=1$0 $\mathrm{~g}$ \sin30^{{}^{\circ}}-$\mathrm{T}-\mu \mathrm{N}$\\ $\text{$ where } $\mathrm{N}=10 \mathrm{~g} \cos30^{{}^{\circ}} \end{array}$
